ops.title: Python-semantics traps in Rust ports (whitespace, dup keys, floats, value preservation)
ops.body:
# Python-semantics traps in Rust ports

Every one of these produced a confirmed parity defect during the v14 P2 ports (found by codex finder passes with reproduced counterexamples). Check each when porting or reviewing.

1. **str whitespace sets differ.** Python `str.strip()`/`split()`/`isspace()` treat `\x1c`–`\x1f` (FS/GS/RS/US), `\x85`, and more as whitespace; Rust `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` (Unicode White_Space) do not. Bit activity twice (blank-prompt detection, hunk normalization). Use the shared core py-whitespace helper (added by the activity lane) — never raw `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` where Python parity matters.
2. **Duplicate JSON object keys.** Python `json.loads` keeps the LAST occurrence (by decoded key, so escaped-equivalents collapse); sonic-rs preserves duplicates and field lookup returns the FIRST. Bit ids (canonicalization) and activity (edit lowering). Use last-wins access for any object field read that mirrors Python dict semantics.
3. **Float formatting ties.** Rust `format!("{:e}")`/`{}`/plain Ryū are NOT ECMAScript/Python-repr tie-exact (counterexample: 698957826421429.2 → Rust `.3`, Python/ES `.2`). Use `ryu-js` for ES-exact output; fuzz new formatting paths against Python (≥10k random bit-pattern doubles). Python `round()` is half-even — mirror it where Python rounds (activity ts_ms).
4. **Value preservation over type-filtering.** Python dataclasses store whatever the JSON carried (`replace_all=1` stays `1`; `description:5` stays `5`; explicit `null` ≠ missing). Rust ports must NOT coerce to typed Options — store loosely (Value) where Python preserves. Bit toolcall across many fields.
5. **Materialization drops.** The Python parse path drops events whose timestamps can't materialize (year-zero, missing ts). Any Rust path that consumes `parse_bytes` directly must apply the same drops or produce phantom events Python never sees. Bit activity_lift. (P3 moves this guard to parse time globally.)
6. **Code-point vs byte string ops.** Python slicing/truncation is code-point-based; Rust byte slicing diverges or panics on multibyte. Any truncation/width logic must mirror Python's exact mechanism.
7. **Big integers.** Python ints are arbitrary precision; i64/u64 conversions or f64 fallbacks lose them. json_to_py projects integer-shaped numbers beyond u64 via int-from-string; canonical_json rejects |int| > 2^53−1 by RAW TOKEN classification (see the digest contract doc 35f43592).
ops.when: porting any Python module to the Rust core, reviewing a Rust parity port, or debugging a Python-vs-Rust parity mismatch
